newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF's Sakakibara says currency moves stable.
newsitem.headline: MOF's Sakakibara says currency moves stable.

text.p: Senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara told a parliamentary committee meeting on Tuesday that exchange rates are now stable as an accord by the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations in late April has filtered through markets.

Asked how he viewed Tuesday's currency moves, Sakakibara told a settlement committee of parliament's Lower House that remarks by Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka at a news conference earlier on Tuesday reflected the ministry's view on exchange rates.
Mitsuzuka said the G7 joint agreement reached in Washington had filtered through the markets and that currencies were stabilising.
The dollar drifted up against the yen in early Tokyo trade on Tuesday, and was hovering around 116.40 by mid-morning.
